name: MonarchPopover
title: Popover
summary: A floating panel anchored to a control, for a small amount of interactive content that belongs to it. Material 3 has no popover, so Monarch builds one on the Compose Popup.
whenToUse: For a filter panel, a quick edit or a short explanation with a link that belongs to one control and should not take the person to another screen.
whenNotToUse: For a list of actions use DropdownMenu (see dropdown-menu). For text that only names a control use a PlainTooltip (see tooltip). For a decision the person must take before going on use AlertDialog (see dialog). For a task with several steps or a long form on a phone use ModalBottomSheet (see sheet).
api: @Composable fun MonarchPopover(expanded: Boolean, onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, label: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, side: MonarchPopoverSide = MonarchPopoverSide.Bottom, content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)

options.name: onDismissRequest
options.description: Called on a tap outside, the back gesture or Escape. Set expanded to false in it.

options.name: label
options.description: The spoken name of the panel, announced when it opens. Start the content with a visible heading too.

options.name: side
options.description: The preferred side of the anchor. The panel moves to the other side when it does not fit.

options.name: content
options.description: The content, in a column with a 12dp gap and 16dp padding. Text takes the default text color.

states.name: closed
states.description: Nothing is drawn; the popup window does not exist.

states.name: open
states.description: The panel fades and grows in over the fast duration below or above the anchor, aligned with its start edge. With animations removed it appears at once.

states.name: no room on the preferred side
states.description: The panel opens on the other side, and is moved inward to keep 16dp from the window edges.

appearance: The panel uses the raised background role with the default text role, a 1dp border in the subtle border role (the strong border role in the high-contrast themes), 12dp corners and the large elevation. Up to 384dp wide, and never wider than the window minus 16dp on each side.
platformNotes: The parity map lists Popover as build on Android and native on iOS, where SwiftUI has popover(isPresented:). It is placed like the Material 3 DropdownMenu: in a Box next to its anchor, whose bounds it uses. The web Popover is non-modal and leaves the page interactive; on Android the popup takes focus, so a tap outside first closes it (the same as iOS). The web's align (start, center, end) and the left and right sides are not offered: phones have little room beside a control, so the panel is start-aligned and opens below or above. The web's PopoverClose is a button that sets expanded to false. The panel has no arrow, as on the web.
accessibility: The panel is a pane with the label as its title, so TalkBack announces it when it opens.
The popup takes focus: TalkBack and keyboard focus move into it, and back, Escape and a tap outside call onDismissRequest.
Controls inside keep their own 48dp touch targets.
Text inside wraps; the panel's width is limited and its height follows the content.
The opening animation is replaced by an immediate change when animations are removed.
edgeCases: At the largest font size a long content can be taller than the screen; put it in a verticalScroll column of limited height, or use a sheet.
If the anchor scrolls away, the panel follows the anchor's position as long as it is composed.
The panel does not close by itself after an action; call onDismissRequest's code from a Done button.
Two popovers open at once each take focus in turn; open one at a time.
